stem:
Asha asks how many 1-digit counting numbers there are.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: There is 1 such number, because a 1-digit number is itself called a digit.
There are 10 such numbers, counting 0 through 9 without the chapter start at 1.
There are 9 such numbers: 1 through 9 each have digit length 1.
The same count also settles how many 2-digit numbers there are, with no further check.

teacher.key_rationale: Digit length is the count of digits in the written form; the chapter counts nine 1-digit numbers from 1 to 9. Calling the answer "1" because the object is named a digit substitutes the wrong label. Counting 0–9 omits the 1-to-9 start. Extending the same count to 2-digit numbers leaves this hinge.
